\subsection{Purpose}




This file defines three execution scenarios for the international job-search roadmap:




\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{Conservative}
\item \textbf{Balanced}
\item \textbf{Aggressive}
\end{enumerate}




The goal is to decide how much risk, volume, salary ambition, contractor exposure, portfolio pressure, and international targeting should be used during the next 3–6 months.




This document does not replace the main strategy. It turns it into selectable operating modes.




\medskip\hrule\medskip

\section{3. Conservative strategy}




\subsection{Definition}




The conservative strategy prioritizes stability, lower risk, realistic first employment, and controlled skill growth.




It aims to secure a first relevant role without overexposing the candidate to risky contractor structures, high-pressure international interviews, or overly senior roles.




\subsection{Best use case}




Use conservative mode if:




\begin{itemize}
\item cashflow pressure becomes high;
\item portfolio is still incomplete;
\item interviews reveal technical gaps;
\item confidence in English interviews is low;
\item legal/admin contractor setup is not ready;
\item there is strong need for stable routine;
\item thesis defense or graduation tasks still consume time.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Portfolio standard}




Minimum required:




\begin{itemize}
\item base CV;
\item LinkedIn updated;
\item TwinSight case study draft;
\item GitHub cleaned enough;
\item 5–8 screenshots;
\item no major public contradictions.
\end{itemize}




Demo video can be draft-quality.




\subsection{Contractor stance}




Conservative mode prefers:




\begin{itemize}
\item clear written contracts;
\item monthly retainer;
\item stable payment terms;
\item LATAM-friendly clients;
\item smaller but safer roles;
\item shorter commitments.
\end{itemize}




Avoid:




\begin{itemize}
\item unpaid tests;
\item equity-only;
\item payment-after-client-approval;
\item ambiguous offshore contracts;
\item broad IP/exclusivity clauses.
\end{itemize}




\subsection{Advantages}




\begin{itemize}
\item Lower probability of severe contract/payment problems.
\item Easier first win.
\item Less interview pressure.
\item More room to continue improving portfolio.
\item Lower risk of burnout.
\end{itemize}




\subsection{Disadvantages}




\begin{itemize}
\item Slower compensation growth.
\item Higher chance of accepting roles below long-term potential.
\item More risk of drifting into generic software/web work.
\item Less exposure to high-value US/EU opportunities.
\end{itemize}




\subsection{Conservative red lines}




Reject if:




\begin{itemize}
\item below USD 1.5k/month unless survival requires it;
\item role is unrelated and consumes full-time capacity;
\item no written contract;
\item no portfolio value;
\item broad non-compete;
\item payment risk high.
\end{itemize}




\subsection{Conservative success definition}




Success after 90 days:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
A stable role or active pipeline around USD 1.5k–3k/month that preserves the Unity / real-time 3D / technical visualization direction.
\end{mdcode}

\section{4. Balanced strategy}




\subsection{Definition}




The balanced strategy combines realistic application volume, strong portfolio positioning, international contractor targeting, and risk control.




It aims to reach the USD 3k/month target within 3–6 months while building toward higher-value roles over 12–24 months.




\subsection{Best use case}




Use balanced mode if:




\begin{itemize}
\item TwinSight case study is publishable;
\item LinkedIn/CV/GitHub are coherent;
\item English interviews are viable;
\item contractor setup can be completed;
\item there is no immediate survival-level cashflow pressure;
\item the goal is better compensation without reckless risk.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Portfolio standard}




Required:




\begin{itemize}
\item polished CV;
\item LinkedIn fully updated;
\item TwinSight case study public or shareable;
\item GitHub cleaned;
\item TwinSight README usable;
\item 8–12 screenshots;
\item 60–90 second demo video or strong draft;
\item ARA positioned correctly;
\item Blender portrait included only if polished.
\end{itemize}




\subsection{Contractor stance}




Balanced mode accepts contractor work if:




\begin{itemize}
\item compensation is above minimum;
\item payment terms are clear;
\item scope is defined;
\item IP is limited to paid work;
\item remote from Colombia is acknowledged;
\item no illegal work authorization assumptions;
\item gross-to-net estimate works.
\end{itemize}




\subsection{Advantages}




\begin{itemize}
\item Best balance of upside and realism.
\item Keeps the profile focused.
\item Builds market feedback quickly.
\item Increases chance of USD 3k/month.
\item Preserves 12–24 month growth path.
\end{itemize}




\subsection{Disadvantages}




\begin{itemize}
\item Requires consistent execution.
\item Requires more outreach and rejection tolerance.
\item Requires contractor admin readiness.
\item Requires stronger interview preparation.
\end{itemize}




\subsection{Balanced red lines}




Reject if:




\begin{itemize}
\item role is full-stack-only with no 3D/Unity relevance;
\item compensation below USD 1.5k/month;
\item unpaid production test;
\item vague contractor terms;
\item company cannot clarify remote/legal structure;
\item role consumes full-time capacity while damaging positioning.
\end{itemize}




\subsection{Balanced success definition}




Success after 90 days:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
A live pipeline of interviews and/or offers in Unity, real-time 3D, technical visualization or WebGL roles, with realistic compensation moving toward USD 3k/month.
\end{mdcode}

\section{5. Aggressive strategy}




\subsection{Definition}




The aggressive strategy prioritizes high-upside international opportunities, direct outreach, speculative applications, contractor positioning, and higher salary negotiation.




It assumes more rejection, more competition, and higher contract risk.




\subsection{Best use case}




Use aggressive mode if:




\begin{itemize}
\item TwinSight case study is strong;
\item demo video is polished;
\item GitHub and LinkedIn are clean;
\item interview answers are rehearsed;
\item contractor/tax setup is ready;
\item cashflow pressure is manageable;
\item the candidate can tolerate rejection and uncertainty;
\item target is USD 4k–6k+/month as soon as possible.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Contractor stance}




Aggressive mode actively targets:




\begin{itemize}
\item higher monthly retainers;
\item USD hourly rates;
\item specialized project contracts;
\item US/EU clients;
\item remote-first companies;
\item studios needing Unity/WebGL/interactive 3D;
\item technical visualization contracts.
\end{itemize}




It also requires stricter risk control.




\subsection{Advantages}




\begin{itemize}
\item Highest income upside.
\item More exposure to strong companies.
\item Faster market feedback.
\item Better chance of reaching USD 3k–6k/month.
\item Stronger professional positioning if successful.
\end{itemize}




\subsection{Disadvantages}




\begin{itemize}
\item More rejection.
\item More unpaid-test attempts.
\item More legal/contract complexity.
\item More senior-role mismatch.
\item Higher emotional load.
\item Greater chance of wasting effort if portfolio is not ready.
\end{itemize}




\subsection{Aggressive red lines}




Reject or pause if:




\begin{itemize}
\item no contract;
\item no clear payment terms;
\item broad IP assignment;
\item unpaid test over reasonable scope;
\item equity-only;
\item role requires false work authorization;
\item company refuses to define remote structure;
\item role demands senior claims you cannot defend;
\item role is outside core positioning.
\end{itemize}




\subsection{Aggressive success definition}




Success after 90 days:




\begin{mdcode}

Multiple active interviews or one high-quality offer in the USD 3k–6k/month range, or strong evidence that the market responds to the Unity/WebGL technical visualization positioning.
\end{mdcode}

\section{7. Scenario triggers}




\subsection{Switch to conservative if}




\begin{itemize}
\item portfolio is not ready after 30 days;
\item cashflow pressure increases;
\item interview rejection shows strong technical gaps;
\item contractor setup is not legally/admin ready;
\item thesis defense demands attention;
\item mental load becomes unsustainable;
\item application volume collapses.
\end{itemize}




\subsection{Stay balanced if}




\begin{itemize}
\item applications are being sent consistently;
\item some recruiter responses appear;
\item portfolio is improving weekly;
\item technical gaps are manageable;
\item salary conversations are near target;
\item rejection is normal but not total silence.
\end{itemize}




\subsection{Switch to aggressive if}




\begin{itemize}
\item TwinSight gets strong feedback;
\item portfolio/demo is polished;
\item recruiter response rate is above 6–10\%;
\item interviews are happening;
\item contractor setup is clear;
\item USD 3k+ conversations are plausible;
\item top A-priority companies show fit.
\end{itemize}




\medskip\hrule\medskip




\section{8. Hybrid recommended strategy}




\subsection{Best practical model}




The optimal path is not purely conservative, balanced or aggressive.




Recommended hybrid:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
Balanced strategy as default.
Aggressive targeting for A-priority companies.
Conservative contract-risk controls.
\end{mdcode}




\subsection{What this means}




Use \textbf{balanced volume}:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
15–30 applications/week
10–25 outreach messages/week
\end{mdcode}




Use \textbf{aggressive targeting} for:




\begin{itemize}
\item technical visualization companies;
\item Unity WebGL roles;
\item digital twin visualization;
\item simulation interfaces;
\item product configurators;
\item XR-adjacent Unity roles;
\item global remote studios.
\end{itemize}




Use \textbf{conservative rules} for:




\begin{itemize}
\item contract review;
\item payment terms;
\item legal status;
\item IP ownership;
\item unpaid tests;
\item relocation;
\item contractor setup.
\end{itemize}




\subsection{Hybrid operating statement}




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
Apply like an ambitious international contractor.
Negotiate like a risk-aware professional.
Position like a focused Unity technical visualization specialist.
\end{mdcode}




\medskip\hrule\medskip

\begin{itemize}
\item polished portfolio;
\item polished TwinSight demo;
\item strong case study;
\item GitHub technical docs;
\item screenshots and diagrams;
\item LinkedIn Featured optimized;
\item interview walkthrough ready;
\item top 30 companies verified.
\end{itemize}




\medskip\hrule\medskip




\section{11. Scenario-specific salary stance}




\subsection{Conservative salary stance}




Use when:




\begin{itemize}
\item role is first relevant job;
\item company is LATAM/local;
\item project fit is strong but budget moderate.
\end{itemize}




Language:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
For remote contractor work, I’m open to discussing compensation based on scope, expected availability and contract structure. My priority is a role with strong fit in Unity, real-time 3D or technical visualization.
\end{mdcode}




Do not anchor too high if the role is clearly lower-budget.




\subsection{Balanced salary stance}




Use by default.




Language:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
For remote contractor work, depending on scope and expected availability, I’m generally targeting the USD 2k–4.5k/month range or an equivalent hourly rate.
\end{mdcode}




Adjust per role.




\subsection{Aggressive salary stance}




Use only for strong-fit US/EU/global roles.




Language:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
For a full-time remote contractor arrangement involving Unity, WebGL, technical visualization and real-time 3D systems, I would generally evaluate compensation in the USD 4k–6k/month range depending on scope, ownership and contract structure.
\end{mdcode}




Do not use aggressive anchors for low-budget LATAM roles.




\medskip\hrule\medskip




\section{12. Scenario-specific red flags}




\subsection{Conservative red flags}




\begin{itemize}
\item low pay plus no portfolio value;
\item local job consuming full-time capacity;
\item unclear contract;
\item unrelated responsibilities.
\end{itemize}




\subsection{Balanced red flags}




\begin{itemize}
\item role slowly becoming generic full-stack;
\item technical visualization not actually part of the work;
\item compensation below USD 1.5k;
\item no contractor clarity;
\item excessive unpaid tests.
\end{itemize}




\subsection{Aggressive red flags}




\begin{itemize}
\item overtargeting senior roles;
\item too much rejection without feedback;
\item unpaid production tasks;
\item high salary but bad contract;
\item US/EU authorization blockers;
\item burnout from high volume.
\end{itemize}




\medskip\hrule\medskip




\section{13. Decision tree}




\subsection{Start here}




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
Is the public portfolio ready enough to explain TwinSight clearly?
\end{mdcode}




If no:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
Use conservative mode for 1–2 weeks.
Finish assets.
\end{mdcode}




If yes:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
Use balanced mode.
\end{mdcode}




Next question:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
Are recruiters/hiring managers responding after 50+ applications/outreach actions?
\end{mdcode}




If no:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
Fix positioning, target list or portfolio top section.
Do not immediately switch roles.
\end{mdcode}




If yes:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
Increase A-priority targeting.
\end{mdcode}




Next question:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
Are salary conversations reaching USD 3k/month or higher?
\end{mdcode}




If no:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
Improve target market and company tier.
Reduce low-value local applications.
\end{mdcode}




If yes:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
Introduce aggressive mode for selected roles.
\end{mdcode}




Next question:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
Are offers safe and strategically aligned?
\end{mdcode}




If no:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
Use offer scorecard and renegotiate/reject.
\end{mdcode}




If yes:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
Accept or negotiate upward.
\end{mdcode}




\medskip\hrule\medskip




\section{14. What each scenario must not do}




\subsection{Conservative must not}




\begin{itemize}
\item become passive;
\item over-focus on local low-pay roles;
\item delay applications forever;
\item accept unrelated work as main strategy;
\item hide from international interviews.
\end{itemize}




\subsection{Balanced must not}




\begin{itemize}
\item try to optimize every asset endlessly;
\item apply to too many unrelated roles;
\item ignore contractor/legal setup;
\item treat USD 3k as impossible;
\item delay outreach.
\end{itemize}




\subsection{Aggressive must not}




\begin{itemize}
\item overclaim seniority;
\item ignore red flags;
\item accept risky contracts for higher gross;
\item pretend current EU authorization exists;
\item burn out through excessive volume;
\item treat rejection as personal failure.
\end{itemize}

\section{17. Risk controls by scenario}




\subsection{Conservative controls}




\begin{itemize}
\item avoid low-quality full-time traps;
\item preserve time for portfolio;
\item do not accept below minimum;
\item do not drop Unity/3D direction.
\end{itemize}




\subsection{Balanced controls}




\begin{itemize}
\item maintain tracker weekly;
\item measure response rates;
\item validate contractor terms;
\item refine based on data;
\item avoid overcustomization.
\end{itemize}




\subsection{Aggressive controls}




\begin{itemize}
\item cap weekly hours;
\item reject exploitative tests;
\item keep legal claims accurate;
\item maintain sleep/routine;
\item review contract risk before accepting;
\item use scorecard objectively.
\end{itemize}
